description: Audience segments is a section in the Audience manager where you can create and manage your data segments.

name: Audience segments section in Audience manager
description: A section of the Audience manager where advertisers can create and manage their data segments, see all segments in one place, view segment type, status and reach per network, and quickly add segments to ad groups and campaigns.

prerequisites: Google tag added to site or app / audience source set up

name: Automatically created segments
description: Google Ads automatically creates some audience segments for the advertiser, including 'All Visitors' and 'All Converters', based on website visitors.

name: Automatically created segments
description: Google Ads automatically creates some audience segments for the advertiser, including the 'All Visitors' and 'All Converters' website visitor segments, and generates segments based on the account's audience sources (for example, conversion-based customer lists).

conditions.detail: Requires a set-up Audience source; auto-generated segments are based on the account's audience sources

name: Caller segments
description: Automatically generated segment tracking people who have already called your business; re-engage them with follow-up ads or exclude them to focus on new leads, with options to target specific ad formats or adjust bids. Individual members cannot be added or removed, and callers appear as a website visitors segment.

name: Callers data segment
description: Tracks people who have already called your business, allowing re-engagement or exclusion from ads. These segments are automatically generated.

name: Callers segments
description: Automatically generated segments tracking people who have already called your business; can be re-engaged with follow-up ads or excluded, with bid adjustments or format targeting. Individual members cannot be added or removed.

name: Conversion-based customer lists

conditions.detail: Requires opting into 'Turn on conversion-based lists'

name: Conversion-based customer lists

For example, if your customer list has the column headers “First Name“, Last Name”, “Country”, “Zip”, and "Phone", each row in your file should have 5 values, each separated by a comma. For scenarios where you have only partial data, like a customer first name but no last name, use a null character in place of the missing value.The following columns in your file have incorrect dataMake sure that the values in your rows correspond with the column header. For example, all of the data in the column titled “Email” should contain valid email addresses only, not zip codes or first names.Column headers in your file are labeled incorrectlyGoogle Ads requires specific column header names, make sure your file is using the correct column header names: “Email”, “Phone", "First Name”, “Last Name”, “Country”, “Zip”, "Phone", and "Mobile Device ID". Postal codes can be used as zip data.

name: Hash data files
description: Google Ads will hash your data file for you if you choose to upload a data file of unhashed customer data in Google Ads. The private customer data in your file (Email, Phone, First Name, and Last Name) will be automatically formatted and hashed on your computer before they are sent securely to Google's servers. The hashing is done locally on the computer that is used to upload the data files, and therefore can be done securely from within an advertiser's own corporate network.If you choose to pre-hash your files:Ensure that you’ve followed the above data file upload best practices before moving on. Low list sizes can be caused by a combination of data file formatting issues and incorrect hashing.Use this Customer Match list formatter toolto validate that your hashing method is correct or to hash your data files.Note:Google is providing this information to you for your own use for hashing data that is to be used for Customer Match. This is meant for informational purposes only and you are solely responsible for how you use it.Once downloaded, open the file in your internet browser. There are three tools available:Hashing Validation - Single Input:Use Case: You're hashing your own data and want to verify the output via a single input. This tool will show you what conversion using the SHA256 algorithm would output. The output from this demo should match the output from your hashing method.Note: Data won’t be scrubbed by this tool prior to hashing (like spaces won’t be removed, letters won’t be lowercase, periods before the @ sign won’t be removed). Scrub your data before you hash to ensure the highest possible match rate.Hashing Demo - CSV output:Use Case: Hash a batch of data from a CSV via upload. The output will be a CSV. Capital letters will be lowercase, spaces and periods before the @ sign will be removed prior to hashing. The output can be uploaded into Google Ads.Hashing Demo - text output:Use Case: Hash a batch of data from a CSV file using copy/paste. The output will be displayed in the right hand side box. Capital letters will be lowercase, spaces will be removed, and periods before the @ sign will be removed prior to hashing. After saving the data as a CSV, it can be uploaded to Google Ads.Or if you use Python,use this scriptto hash your data files

name: Troubleshoot low traffic
description: “No or low volume” is often caused by too small of a list, too narrow of targeting, and/or low bids or budget compared to other remarketing campaigns.For Customer Match ads to serve, they must have a minimum threshold of active users at the time the ad is served (active users are the number of users on your list that are active on Gmail, Search, YouTube, or Display). At any given time, the number of active users will likely be less than your total audience list size - not everyone is signed in all the time.We recommend audience list sizes of at least 100 users to prevent ads from not serving.Any additional targeting restrictions you add on top of the Customer Match list will further narrow down the audience list of potential users your campaign can target, ultimately leading to low or no volume.

name: Ad Strength for responsive search ads
description: Ad Strength is a quality signal for responsive search ads; Google recommends at least 2 RSAs with 'Good' or 'Excellent' Ad Strength per ad group, citing 15% more clicks & conversions on average when improving from 'Poor' to 'Excellent'.

name: Ad Strength rating
description: Ad Strength rates responsive search ads from 'Poor' to 'Excellent'; Google advises implementing at least 2 RSAs with 'Good' or 'Excellent' Ad Strength per ad group, reports that improving Ad Strength from 'Poor' to 'Excellent' correlates with 15% more clicks and conversions on average, and notes that pinning can affect Ad Strength.

name: Asset and combination reporting

name: Automatic ad combination testing
description: After headlines and descriptions are entered, Google Ads assembles them into multiple ad combinations in a way that avoids redundancy, tests the most promising ad combinations over time, and learns which combinations are the most relevant for different queries.

name: Automatic ad combination testing
description: Google Ads automatically tests the most promising ad combinations over time and learns which combinations are most relevant for different queries; RSA headlines may also be bolded when matching search queries.

name: Automatic bold text matching
description: Part of the responsive search ad text may automatically appear in bold when it matches or closely matches a user's search query.

name: Enhanced Flexibility
description: Responsive search ad assets can serve beyond the traditional headline positions based on what is predicted to perform best for each person's unique search query: headline asset text may show at the beginning of the description; up to 2 unused headlines within the same ad can serve as link-based assets (in the space that previously only sitelinks were eligible for), pointing to the same domain as the ad's final URL, with RSA description lines also able to serve in the link-based asset description space; and unused headlines and description assets from another ad in the same ad group can serve as link-based assets pointing to that RSA's final ad URL.

conditions.detail: Only active ads and assets are eligible for enhanced flexibility

name: Pin headlines and descriptions to positions

Text pinned to Headline position 1 or 2 or Description position 1 always shows; content pinned to Headline position 3 or Description position 2 is not guaranteed to show in every ad. Pinning reduces the number of headlines or descriptions that can be matched to a search and can affect Ad Strength, while Google optimizes the placement of all other (unpinned) assets.

name: Pin headlines and descriptions to specific positions

name: Responsive search ad performance reporting

Reports can be downloaded in formats such as .csv or .pdf, opened in Report Editor, scheduled, or emailed.

name: Responsive search ads
description: Ad format where the advertiser enters multiple headlines (minimum 3, up to 15) and descriptions (minimum 2, up to 4) plus a final URL and display path text, and Google Ads assembles them into multiple ad combinations that adapt to more closely match potential customers' search terms and device widths, letting the ads compete in more auctions. Headline fields support up to 30 characters, descriptions up to 90, and path fields up to 15 each, with each character in double-width languages such as Korean, Japanese, or Chinese counting as 2. In any given ad a minimum of one headline and one description is selected; usually Headline 1 and Description 1 appear, additional headlines and descriptions may appear based on predicted performance or available space and are not guaranteed, and text may be shortened, usually with an ellipsis.

name: Responsive search ads

name: Ad group-level Target CPA targets

name: Average target CPA metric

Found in the performance table at the top of the Campaigns page (selectable as the 'Avg. target CPA' column or chart metric) and in bid strategy reports beside 'Actual CPA'. Available for both standard and portfolio bid strategies; no value exists for periods without traffic, and Google recommends measuring periods with at least 30 conversions. App campaigns use the 'Avg. target cost per install' and 'Avg. target cost per in-app action' variants.

name: Target CPA bidding

name: Target CPA bidding
description: Automated bid strategy that sets bids each time an ad is eligible to appear, using historical campaign information and auction-time contextual and real-time signals (device, browser, location, time of day, remarketing list) to get as many conversions or customer actions as possible at the advertiser's desired average cost per conversion. Some conversions may cost more or less than the target, but Google Ads tries to keep average cost per conversion at the target. Usable with no conversion history, effective for campaigns of all sizes, and available as a standard strategy on a single campaign or as a portfolio strategy across multiple campaigns.

conditions.detail: Conversion tracking must be set up before you can set up a Target CPA bid strategy

name: Target CPA device bid adjustments
description: Device bid adjustments for Target CPA let the advertiser prioritize conversions by device, with adjustments settable for desktop, tablet, and mobile. Unlike manual CPC, the adjustments modify the value of the CPA target rather than the bids themselves (e.g., a +40% mobile adjustment raises a $10 target to $14 on mobile), and a -100% mobile adjustment prevents ads from showing on mobile devices. Google suggests removing manual CPC bid adjustments when switching to Target CPA, and notes that non-device bid adjustments are ignored on the Search and Display Network.

name: Learning mode
description: Learning mode is a testing phase where ads are shown to different types of people to identify who is most likely to convert, with campaign performance potentially fluctuating during this period.

name: Learning mode
description: After a campaign is created, Pinterest shows the ads to different types of people to learn who is most likely to convert, and campaign performance may fluctuate during this phase. Once Learning mode has completed with enough data, ads are shown to the people most likely to convert and performance should stabilise. It varies by each unique advertiser with no set time horizon and is removed when the system finds that conversion events have stabilised.

conditions.detail: Learning mode is still in testing and is gradually being rolled out to all audiences.

name: Conversions API event tracking
description: Track conversion events - actions customers take in person or online - by sending events from websites, apps, or offline sources such as store locations to the ad account's events endpoint (POST /v5/ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/events). Required server event fields include action_source, event_id, event_name, and event_time (Unix timestamp in seconds).

conditions.detail: The Conversions API endpoint requires a unique identifier associated with the ad account that is sending events - a Pinterest advertiser account.
Requires a conversion token for Conversions API-only access, or an OAuth token with at least ads:write scopes to access other API endpoints.
The ad_account ID is required for the request path.
user_data object must include at least one of hashed_maids or a pairing of client_ip_address and client_user_agent.
Pass event_id and event_name in all ingestion sources with an identical event_id for each redundant event.
Batch limit of 1000 events per request.
Test event batches are limited to the first 20 events processed.
Up to 15 custom event types can be defined per advertiser ID.
partner_id is only for Pinterest integration partners.
Only send the np field if Pinterest has worked directly with you to define a partner_name value.
Custom events must be mapped to a Pinterest standard event.
To interact with tools/endpoints related to campaigns, ad groups, and ads, the OAuth token must be related to a Pinterest advertiser ID.
Requires a Pinterest advertiser account and a conversion token, or an OAuth token with at least ads:write scope, to send events via the Conversions API.
The pairing of client_ip_address and client_user_agent is one of the accepted minimum identifiers required in the user_data object (the other is hashed_maids).
